source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design: Islamic Religious Education, Grade 7
source.notes: First Published 2023, Revised 2024, ISBN 978-9914-43-926-7. Read directly via the Read tool (no pages param) per CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md. Strand/sub-strand headings, SLOs, learning experiences (including verbatim parenthetical lists), key inquiry questions, core competencies, values, PCIs and links to other subjects transcribed from the strand tables (pp.1-38). Community Service Learning (pp.39-46) is a milestone-based practical activity hosted in Social Studies, not covered by generated practice skills, same treatment as g7-ss-csl in social-studies.json.

subStrands.name: 1.1 Ulumul Qur'an
specificLearningOutcomes: Discuss the rationale for the revelation of the Qur'an as a guide to mankind
Describe the stages of revelation of the Qur'an as a sign of mercy to mankind
Describe the incident of the first revelation of the Qur'an at cave Hira to show the importance of seeking knowledge
Explain the reasons for the revelation of the Qur'an in portions for ease of its implementation
Assess the importance of the Qur'an in day-to-day life of a Muslim as a divine guidance for humanity
Value the Qur'an as a book of guidance to mankind
keyInquiryQuestions: Why was the Qur'an revealed to mankind?
How does the Qur'an guide mankind?
How did Muslims benefit from the revelation of the Qur'an in portions?
learningExperiences: Research online/on available reference materials on the rationale for the revelation of the Qur'an and make a class presentation
Discuss the stages of the revelation of the Qur'an in groups and make notes
Search and watch videos on the first incident at cave Hira and narrate individually in class
Research on the reasons for the revelation of the Qur'an in portions and make class presentation
Discuss on the importance of the Qur'an in pairs and make notes
linkedLearningAreas: Pre-technical Studies — skills of interacting with digital technology during search for, and watching videos on the incident of the first revelation at cave Hira
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric distinguishes 'discusses the revelation correctly and comprehensively' from 'correctly' — full stage sequence (not just headline fact) is expected at Meets Expectations.

subStrands.name: 1.2 Selected Chapters (Surah)
specificLearningOutcomes: Read surah Ad-Dhuha (Q.93:1-11) and surah Al-Balad (Q.90:1-20) correctly for spiritual nourishment
Explain the meaning of surah Ad-Dhuha (Q.93:1-11) and surah Al-Balad (Q.90:1-20) for better understanding
Discuss the teachings/lessons of surah Ad-Dhuha (Q.93:1-11) and surah Al-Balad (Q.90:1-20) for application in daily life
Apply the teachings of surah Ad-Dhuha (Q.93:1-11) and surah Al-Balad (Q.90:1-20) in their daily life to earn rewards from Allah
Appreciate the teachings of surah Ad-Dhuha (Q.93:1-11) and surah Al-Balad (Q.90:1-20) as a guide in daily life
keyInquiryQuestions: What lessons do Muslims learn from the selected surah?
How can a Muslim apply the teachings of the selected surah?
learningExperiences: Read the selected surah
Discuss the meaning of the selected surah in groups and make class presentations
Research on the teachings/lessons from selected surah online/on available reference materials in pairs and make class presentations
Dramatize teachings/lessons from Surah Ad-Dhuha (treatment of orphans, needy and bounties of Allah)
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts — dramatizing teachings/lessons from surah Ad-Dhuha (treatment of orphans, needy, appreciating bounties of Allah)
scopeNotes: include: Surah Ad-Dhuha teachings named explicitly — treatment of orphans, respect for parents, humility, appreciating Allah's bounties
subStrands.notes: Split into two skills (surahAdDuha.ts, surahAlBalad.ts) given the 12-lesson depth and each surah having distinct, substantial verse content.

subStrands.name: 2.1 Ulumul Hadith
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the meaning of hadith for better understanding

State the components of Hadith for better understanding of science of Hadith
Explain the types of Hadith (Hadith Qudsy and Nabawy) as the second source of Sharia
Assess the importance of Hadith for spiritual nourishment

Acknowledge Hadith as a primary source of Sharia
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is Hadith important in the life of a Muslim?
learningExperiences: Search online/on available reference materials on the meaning of hadith
Discuss on the components of Hadith in groups and present in class
Research on forms of Hadith (Qaul, Fiil, Taqrir, Sifat) and prepare a chart for display in groups
Research on types of Hadith (Nabawy and Qudsy) and make class presentation
Discuss the differences between Hadith Qudsy and Nabawy in groups and share in class
Research on the importance of hadith from available reference materials and make notes

subStrands.name: 2.2 Selected Hadith
subStrands.notes: Hadith on intention (Umar bin Khattab R.A., Bukhari and Muslim) and Hadith on choice of friends (Abu Musa R.A., Bukhari and Muslim) — full texts transcribed verbatim below.

hadithTexts.text: I heard the Prophet (S.A.W.) say, actions are judged by intentions and everyone will get what was intended. So, the one whose hijrah was to Allah and His Messenger, then his hijrah was to Allah and His Messenger. The one whose hijrah was for the world to gain from it, or a woman to marry, then his hijrah was to what he made hijrah for.

The example of a good companion (who sits with you) in comparison with a bad one, is like that of the musk seller and the blacksmith's bellows (or furnace); from the first you would either buy musk or enjoy its good smell while the bellows would either burn your clothes or your house, or you get a bad nasty smell thereof.

specificLearningOutcomes: Discuss the lessons learnt from the selected Hadith for character building
Explain the relevance of the selected Hadith in the life of a Muslim
Practise the teachings from the selected hadith in daily life
Appreciate Hadith as the second source of Islamic law and spiritual guidance
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the benefits of having good intention?
Who is a good friend?
Why is it important to choose good friends?
learningExperiences: Read the selected hadith
Discuss lessons derived from the selected hadith in pairs or groups and make class presentation
Discuss the relevance of the selected Hadith in the life of a Muslim and make notes
Role play the qualities and importance of having good friends
Create social groups with friends where they can share information to influence each other positively
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — role playing the qualities of good friends

subStrands.name: 4.1 Swalah
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe how congregational prayers and sunnah prayers are performed to earn rewards (Tahajud, Tahiyatul Masjid and Dhuha)

Perform congregational prayers, sunnah prayers and prayers on special occasions for spiritual nourishment

Why are Sunnah prayers important?

Demonstrate the performance of congregational prayers, Sunnah prayers and prayers on special occasions

linkedLearningAreas: Integrated Science — Swalatul Kusuf and Khusuf relate to knowledge on eclipses
scopeNotes: include: named sunnah prayers are Tahajud, Tahiyatul Masjid, Dhuha; named special-occasion prayers are Swalatul Janaza (funeral), Musafir (traveller), Kusuf (solar eclipse), Khusuf (lunar eclipse)

Search for the differences between Zakatul Maal and Zakatul Fitr and present on charts/posters/PowerPoint
Research on items exempted from Zakat in groups and make class presentation
linkedLearningAreas: Pre-technical Studies — business skills relating to identifying items exempted from Zakat and discussing the importance of zakat

subStrands.name: 4.3 Saum
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe types of Saum for ease of observance (Fardh, Sunnah, Nadhir, Kafara, Qadha)

keyInquiryQuestions: What are the benefits of Saum in the life of a Muslim?
learningExperiences: Discuss the types of Saum, make charts in groups and present in class
Research on the significance of Saum and present on PowerPoint/charts in groups

scopeNotes: include: five named types of Saum — Fardh (obligatory), Sunnah (recommended), Nadhir (vow), Kafara (expiation), Qadha (makeup)

subStrands.name: 7.1 Reforms introduced By Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.)

learningExperiences: Search online for video clips/available reference materials on the Jahiliyya period
Discuss the socio-religious, political and economic reforms introduced by Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) in groups and make class presentation
Watch/read and make a comparative analysis between Jahiliyya and post Jahiliyya periods and make notes
Discuss the importance of socio-religious, political and economic reforms introduced by Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) in groups and make class presentation

subStrands.notes: 16-lesson sub-strand, the deepest in Grade 7 IRE alongside Swalah (10) and Selected Chapters (12) — reforms span socio-religious, political AND economic dimensions plus an explicit Jahiliyya vs post-Jahiliyya comparative-analysis outcome; all three dimensions and the comparison must be covered, not just a headline 'reforms were good' summary.
